$comment: Execution-loop bookkeeping for automated contributors. Not consumed by the
crate at build or run time; nothing in src/ or tests/ reads this file.
Kept in-tree so a later cycle (or a different session) can see what has
already been tried and, more importantly, what was tried and REJECTED —
the rejected list is the part that stops cycles rediscovering the same

verified_against.note: This crate declares NO [features]; `--all-features` is a no-op here. The authoritative gate is scripts/gate.sh, which spans several workflow files and includes the rustdoc-lint and MSRV passes that reconstructing from ci.yml alone drops.

completed_slots.outcome: PR #315 repaired and merged. Red since 2026-08-02 on one rustdoc error; root cause was structural, not a typo: a commit inserted `struct AbortOnDrop` between `TrackedEntityMap`'s 26-line doc comment and the struct, so AbortOnDrop adopted another type's documentation and `Self::take_dirty` could not resolve. Moved the block back rather than rewriting the link. 5 merge conflicts resolved per-hunk on evidence.

PRs #302 and #305 closed: both descend from root fed9a5e7 while main descends from 9ec08790, so `git merge-tree` reports 'refusing to merge unrelated histories' and GitHub could never have merged them. Both also register FEWER modules than main (167 and 166 vs 169). PR #317 deliberately kept OPEN: it registers 173 modules and carries builtwith/fofa/proxycurl/key_discovery, none of which exist in main.

oathnet door-guard completeness. Copilot's finding on #362 confirmed against source. #363 landed the equivalent code fix in parallel, so #364 narrowed to what #363 shipped without: the pinning test, a fix for a pre-existing test-suite race (reset_budget clears RESPONSE_CACHE, racing the cache tests), and the rate-limit misdiagnosis #363's change made reachable.

cycle_1_slots.instruction: Decide and record the DbWriter unbounded-channel question (OD-1).
cycle_1_slots.status: COMPLETE — DECIDED: keep the channel unbounded, and disclose a pathological backlog. Bounding it would force try_send (drops events, breaking the flush() contract) or an async submit() at a sync engine call site. The queue is also already bounded in practice by DEFAULT_MAX_ENTITIES=2500 and the wall-time watchdog. The real defect was that a storage stall was INVISIBLE, so writer_loop now discloses queue depth past BACKLOG_WARN_EVENTS=1024 with hysteresis at half.

observations.summary: `cargo tree --duplicates` reports getrandom at v0.2.17, v0.3.4 and v0.4.3. All three are transitive and not directly reachable from this crate's manifest: 0.2 via ring -> rustls -> reqwest, 0.3 via proptest -> rand_core (a dev-dependency only), 0.4 separately. Deduplicating would mean forcing versions on ring/rustls, which is a larger risk than the duplication.
observations.action: none — recorded so a later cycle does not re-derive it

open_defects.summary: DbWriter uses mpsc::unbounded_channel (src/core/engine/writer.rs:39). If event production outpaces sqlite batch writes the queue grows without bound, on a platform whose whole point is a memory-constrained no-root Android device. Exposure INCREASED when #315 raised DEFAULT_SCAN_DEPTH 3->5, since more rounds means more events.
open_defects.status: CLOSED cycle 1 slot 5 — resolved as a disclosure, not a bound. See src/core/engine/writer.rs module docs for why unbounded is correct here and what actually bounds it.
